contentBlocks.text: This week you built a complete media-literacy toolkit — evaluation, AI-content awareness, verification, and perspective-awareness. Let's apply all of it at once.

Quick review: a strong evaluation asks purpose, evidence, and missing context (Day 1). AI-generated content shows some signals, though none are definitive proof alone (Day 2). Lateral reading verifies claims against independent sources, rather than judging a source by its own presentation (Day 3). Perspective and bias shape coverage even when facts are accurate, which is exactly why comparing sources matters (Day 4). Choose one new piece of media you haven't evaluated yet this week, and apply the complete framework: its purpose, its evidence, whether it shows any AI-content signals, what an independent source says about its key claim, and what perspective it represents.

Excellent work this week — you now have a genuine, complete media-literacy toolkit, not just isolated skills. This is exactly the critical-evaluation foundation your capstone research project later this year will depend on.

objectives: Synthesize the week's four skills — evaluation framework, AI-content awareness, lateral reading, perspective-awareness — into one complete analysis
Apply the complete framework to a new piece of media
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child pick a new piece of media and apply the complete framework.
3. Complete the cumulative review worksheet.
4. Discuss any uncertain answers together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing the first full week of Grade 12 ELA — this framework underpins the capstone research project ahead.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to apply the framework to a shorter or simpler piece of media, focused on hitting all five required elements rather than depth on each
Ready for more: ask them to identify which single skill from this week (evaluation, AI-awareness, lateral reading, or perspective-awareness) was most useful for their chosen piece of media, and why
This is a good checkpoint to note which part of the media-literacy toolkit needs the most re-teaching before the capstone research unit begins
teacherGuide.answerKey: A complete answer applies all four skills to one new piece of media: its purpose and evidence, whether it shows AI-content signals, what an independent source says about its key claim via lateral reading, and what perspective it represents — content varies genuinely by student, evaluated against these required elements.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates the course's 'media/AI literacy' description before the unit moves toward the capstone research project and independent literature study, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.
